tests.description: A handler that changes the disk while it answers a question has changed it before the first step runs, because every question is raised before anything runs. The later tests in this file change the disk this way.

A narrow line runs a step at a time and prints what one bash -c of the whole line printed: `;` runs the next step whatever the last one did, `&&` and `||` skip by the last status, `$?` reads the status of the step before, a cd moves the steps after it, a group's cd ends at its parenthesis, and the line fails with the last step's status. These values were recorded while the whole line still ran under one shell.

tests.description: A cd inside a group whose folder is gone when it runs is not the folder that was approved, so the line stops there, and neither the group's ls nor the ls sub after the group runs.

Each row: the line, whether it succeeded, whether it stopped, and whether anything from the outside folder was printed. A file or folder swapped for a link to the outside folder after approval makes the step that names it plan to something else just before it runs, so the line stops before that step and prints nothing from outside. With nothing swapped the line runs, and the timeout field alone in a std::exec payload stops nothing.
tests.expectedOutput: [["pnpm --version; wc -l one.txt",false,true,false],["pnpm --version; ls sub",false,true,false],["pnpm --version; wc -l one.txt",true,false,false]]

tests.description: A stop is a failure of type planChanged. Its text ends with a sentence that names the step as the model wrote it, then the status line the agent's trace reads.

The check plans each step with a fresh line, which knows nothing of what the steps before it wrote or made. A folder the line made, a cd into it, a file the line wrote, and a second write to that file all plan to what was approved, so none of these lines stops. Neither does a listing of a folder a program made, which was missing when the plan was made, nor a listing of a file the line wrote.
tests.expectedOutput: [["mkdir -p out && ls out",true,false],["mkdir -p build && cd build && pnpm --version",true,false],["pnpm --version > v.txt && cat v.txt",true,false],["pnpm --version > v.txt; pnpm --version >> v.txt",true,false],["node -e \"require('fs').mkdirSync('d')\" && ls d",true,false],["pnpm --version > v.txt; ls -la v.txt",true,false]]

tests.description: A gh read that names no repository is planned again with the repository the up-front lookup found, so the check does not stop it.

Each row: the line, whether it succeeded, the step it stopped before, and whether the outside repository's status was printed. A folder swapped for a link to another repository after approval stops the line before the cd that enters it, and before a step that runs in it from the start, where the step's own payload names the folder as an unchanged string. With nothing swapped the line runs.
tests.expectedOutput: [["git status; cd sub && git status",false,"cd sub",false],["cd sub && pnpm --version",false,"cd sub",false],["cd sub && ls",true,"",false],["git status; git log --oneline -1",false,"git status",false]]

tests.description: Each row: the line, whether it succeeded, the step it stopped before, and whether anything from outside was printed. A git checkout that puts a link where a file or folder was is narrow, and the step that names the swapped path stops the line before it runs. Narrow questions are approved and the broad one rejected, so a checkout and a read in one group of a pipeline, which run as one step, ask std::bash and run nothing.
tests.expectedOutput: [["git checkout evil; wc -l one.txt",false,"wc -l one.txt",false],["git checkout evil && ls sub",false,"ls sub",false],["git checkout evil && cd sub && git status",false,"cd sub",false],["(git checkout evil && cat one.txt) | cat",false,"",false]]

tests.description: The folder check compares real folders, so a line planned in ".", in a folder spelled through a link, or in a relative folder does not stop when nothing changed.
The time limit covers the whole line: three steps under a 2 second limit stop at 2 seconds in total.
Once the limit has run out, no later step starts: the write after the step that used up the time never runs.
A line with a variable in an echo runs to the end: the std::env question sits on the echo's step, so the plan made just before the step asks it again and matches what was approved.
Two commands that read the same variable ask std::env for it once. The row is the questions asked, whether the line succeeded, and whether ran.txt exists.

Every question is asked before anything runs, so when std::env is rejected the line fails and the write before the echo never happens: ran.txt does not exist. The row is the questions asked, whether the line succeeded, and whether ran.txt exists.

Each row: the line, whether safeBash runs each step itself (with "cd" for a cd and a list for a group), and the questions asked. A cat, a grep, or an echo is run by safeBash wherever it sits in the line, and bash runs the steps beside it. A pipeline, a command behind timeout, and a read of a file that does not exist when the line is planned stay with bash.
tests.expectedOutput: [["pnpm --version; cat one.txt",[false,true],["std::exec","std::read"]],["cat one.txt && pnpm --version",[true,false],["std::read","std::exec"]],["cd sub && cat a.txt",["cd",true],["std::read"]],["(pnpm --version && cat one.txt)",[[false,true]],["std::exec","std::read"]],["pnpm --version > made.txt; cat made.txt",[false,false],["std::exec","std::write","std::read"]],["timeout 5 cat one.txt",[false],["std::read"]],["cat one.txt | head -1",[false],["std::read"]],["pnpm --version; grep -n one one.txt",[false,true],["std::exec","std::grep"]],["pnpm --version; echo hi > out.txt",[false,true],["std::exec","std::write"]]]

tests.description: The payload describes what runs. A search safeBash runs itself after a program asks std::grep with the limit of 1000 matches and the flag the stdlib search uses. An echo into a file after a program asks std::write with the text. A cat after a cd names the folder the cd moved to.

Each row: the line, whether it succeeded, and its text. A line that mixes steps bash runs with steps safeBash runs itself prints each step's output in order, and a later step sees the status the step before it left: `echo $?` after a cat prints 0, after a grep that matched nothing prints 1, and `||` after that grep runs its right side.

tests.description: Each row: the line, whether it succeeded, whether it stopped, and whether anything from the outside folder was printed. A file or a folder swapped for a link to the outside folder after approval fails a cat that safeBash runs itself, because the read tool refuses a link in the path it opens. The line fails with no stop and prints nothing from outside.

Every question is asked before anything runs, so when the std::read of a cat is rejected the program before it never runs: ran.txt does not exist. The row is the questions asked, whether the line succeeded, and whether ran.txt exists.
